target_customer: Women and the clinics, breast imaging centers and physicians who screen or monitor them, including point-of-care, walk-in and mobile clinics
problem: Handheld breast ultrasound depends on operator skill and is hard to repeat or scale, so supplemental breast imaging is limited. iSono automates a whole-breast 3D scan with a wearable device.
business_model: Medical device sales to clinics plus software and AI analysis (ATUSA system), early partner program for paying clinics
product_category: Automated wearable 3D breast ultrasound with AI

founders.name: Shadi Saberi
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder/CTO on the YC page. No background found in opened sources.

founders.name: Neda Razavi
founders.background_notes: Named as CEO in the January 2026 launch article. That article does not call her a founder and the YC page does not list her, so her founder status is unconfirmed. A search snippet from a third site names Maryam Ziaei as CEO and cofounder, which conflicts and is unverified.

technical_complexity.rationale: A custom ultrasound transducer scan mechanism, 3D reconstruction, cloud processing and AI on acoustic biomarkers, plus FDA 510(k) clearance, which came in 2022, six years after founding.

defensibility.rationale: The company describes the scanner as patented and the ATUSA system holds FDA 510(k) clearance, both slow to replicate. The AI features are described by the company as investigational only.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source opened shows an incumbent copying or buying the wedge by 2026. The company remained independent.

market_need_then: The company pitches radiation-free, operator-independent imaging for early detection. No dated 2015 or 2016 demand evidence was found in opened sources.

identity.voice_and_tone: Clinical, device-focused product language with the ATUSA product name

brand_strength.rationale: Search found trade press only about product launches and clearance, nothing about the brand itself. Spelling varies between iSono and Isono across sources.

outcome_analysis: iSono has stayed independent for a decade while building a hard hardware and AI product. It won FDA 510(k) clearance for ATUSA in 2022, raised a $3M seed in 2025 and in January 2026 announced a commercial launch with a Series A open. Progress is slow and capital light for a medical device, with the company citing $14.7M raised in total and a further $3.7M in non-dilutive grants, so the story is a long regulatory climb rather than a breakout or a failure.
notes: Company states $14.7M raised in total including $3M in 2025 and $3.7M non-dilutive grants from NIH, NSF and NCI, so earlier rounds exist that are not itemized in opened sources. A search snippet from an aggregator mentions a 2019 seed led by Foothill Ventures with ATO Ventures, DHVC and Camford Capital; amount unknown and unverified, so not recorded as a round. Third-party trackers disagree widely on totals ($1.8M to $25M). Sources disagree on whether the 2025 round was led by Draper and Transform VC or by JSK. FDA clearance dated March or April 2022 depending on source. No dated competitor sources near the 2016 batch were found, so the list is empty. Series A was open as of January 2026 and is not a closed round.
